newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen signs oil deals with U.S.,British companies.
newsitem.headline: Yemen signs oil deals with U.S.,British companies.

text.p: Yemen on Thursday signed three memoranda of understanding with U.S. and British firms to set up oil exploration projects, an official source at the Yemeni oil ministry said.
"Two memoranda of understanding were signed with the U.S. company Kerr-McGee Corp to explore for oil in sectors 50, 51 and 54 in the Shabwa governorate (former South Yemen)," the source told Reuters.
"(Another) memorandum of understanding was signed with the British company Dove to start oil exploration in sector number 53 in Shabwa governorate," he said.

He said the Yemeni government would contribute 25 percent to the project cost in sector 53, starting at the beginning of the explorations. Yemen usually reaches agreements to contribute to the projects only once oil has been found.
The source did not give the exact cost of the projects or say when they would start. He gave no further details.
The memoranda still have to be approved by the cabinet to become official agreements.
Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the Arab world and is dependent on its oilfields, which produce about 365,000 barrels per day.
